report.source_text: Light microscopy showed moderate to severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma. The periodic acid-Schiff staining showed moderate to diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma ( Figure 1A ), and the periodic acid silver methenamine staining and Masson’s staining showed severe diffuse proliferation of mesangial cells and stroma ( Figure 1B ). It was accompanied by diffuse thickening of the basement membrane, small eosinophilic deposits in the subendothelial segment, and microangioma-like expansion of segmental capillary loops. There were vacuoles and granular degeneration of renal tubular epithelial cells, focal atrophy, and a few protein casts were observed in the lumen. Renal interstitial focal lymphocyte and monocyte infiltration with fibrosis, wall thickening of small arteries, intimal fibrosis and sclerosis, and lumen stenosis were also observed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old retired male with 26-year history of diabetes mellitus and 20-year history of hypertension presented with one year of intermittent facial and bilateral lower extremity edema, increased nocturia, and proteinuria. On admission, routine urinalysis showed proteinuria (3+), hematuria (RBC 0.61/Hp), and glycosuria (2+). Laboratory studies revealed preserved renal function (creatinine 57 μmol/L, BUN 7.63 mmol/L), nephrotic-range proteinuria (5.54 g/24h), and hypoalbuminemia (30 g/L). Renal biopsy performed on 10 November 2021 confirmed IgA nephropathy Type IIa. Immunofluorescence microscopy demonstrated IgA-dominant deposits with C3 co-deposition (IgA+, IgG±, C3+, C1q-). Light microscopy showed moderate to severe diffuse mesangial proliferation with basement membrane thickening, subendothelial deposits, tubular degeneration, and interstitial fibrosis. Electron microscopy revealed mild to moderate mesangial proliferation, homogeneous glomerular basement membrane thickening, mesangial electron-dense deposits, and segmental foot process fusion. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone 32 mg daily for three months with prophylactic isoniazid, resulting in partial relief of nephrotic syndrome.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While patient has 26-year history of diabetes, the renal biopsy findings of IgA-dominant deposits on immunofluorescence with mesangial proliferation are characteristic of primary IgA nephropathy, not diabetic glomerulosclerosis. The immunofluorescence pattern (IgA+ dominant, C1q-) is inconsistent with diabetic nephropathy.

Although patient has 20-year hypertension history, the renal biopsy with IgA-dominant immunofluorescence deposits and mesangial proliferation is diagnostic of IgA nephropathy, not hypertensive arteriolosclerosis.

The immunofluorescence pattern (IgA+ dominant, C1q-, no mention of anti-GBM or ANCA positivity) and the clinical presentation are consistent with primary IgA nephropathy rather than secondary forms. C1q negativity argues against lupus nephritis.
